selection_method: SequenceMatcher stem ratio identifies candidate only; actual direct reading needed

records.stem:
Case A: For a proposed federal emergency oral Schedule II prescription, the prescriber's receptionist calls a certified technician instead of the prescribing practitioner speaking to the pharmacist.

Case B: A central-fill pharmacy proposes accepting the emergency oral prescription directly under the ordinary retail emergency pathway.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The pharmacist may dispense first and postpone all oral-order recording until the follow-up arrives.
A central-fill pharmacy may accept the emergency oral Schedule II order through the same retail pathway.
The specified federal emergency pathway requires the prescribing individual practitioner to authorize the pharmacist.
An unknown caller's assertion of being a prescriber removes the need for authenticity verification.

records.stem:
Case A: A valid Schedule II prescription is faxed for a resident of a qualifying long-term-care facility.

Case B: A separate hospice fax concerns a Schedule II nonnarcotic drug, and staff invoke the hospice-narcotic exception without considering whether another lawful pathway applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described federal LTCF fax-as-original route is not limited to narcotic Schedule II drugs.
Any informal description of comfort care necessarily establishes the qualifying hospice fax pathway.
The hospice-narcotic exception itself covers every Schedule II drug regardless of narcotic status.
Fax-as-original status removes all other prescription requirements.

records.stem:
Case A: A faxed Schedule II narcotic prescription is for a compounded parenteral infusion meeting the specified route and direct-administration conditions.

Case B: Staff extend that exception to any Schedule II injectable product, without checking whether it is a narcotic or a qualifying compounded infusion.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Meeting the infusion fax exception permits otherwise prohibited Schedule II refills.
Any Schedule II injectable automatically qualifies without the narcotic or compounding conditions.
The fax exception applies to any oral tablet merely because the patient also receives an infusion.
The first case must be evaluated under the specific compounded-infusion fax exception.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy provides a shortage-based Schedule II partial fill on Monday at 2 p.m.; all remaining conditions are valid, and the remainder is available Thursday at noon.

Case B: For a second shortage-based partial fill, the remainder becomes available 80 hours after the first partial dispensing.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Receiving new inventory starts a fresh 72-hour remainder period.
The shortage clock necessarily starts at the issue date instead of the first partial fill.
Thursday at noon is within 72 hours of the first case's Monday 2 p.m. partial fill.
The second remainder may be supplied at 80 hours merely because the original prescription has not otherwise expired.

records.stem:
Case A: An adult patient requests less than the prescribed Schedule II quantity on day 20 after issuance, and the pharmacy begins a qualifying request-based partial fill.

Case B: A casual pickup agent asks for a larger partial amount than the prescriber specified and claims that pickup authority is sufficient.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The initial partial and each remainder must be recorded with the relevant quantities and dates.
The general request-based remainder clock is tied to issuance, not a new 30 days from day 20.
A printed partial-fill notice establishes a patient request even when no request occurred.
Pickup status alone does not establish the specified request authority or permission to exceed the prescriber's partial amount.

records.stem:
Case A: An emergency oral Schedule II prescription is partially filled at the patient's request, and staff apply the ordinary nonemergency 30-day requested-partial window.

Case B: A Massachusetts patient asks a different pharmacy in the same chain to provide a remainder after an initial requested partial fill at the first pharmacy.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The federal emergency-oral requested-partial remainder limit is 72 hours from issuance rather than the ordinary 30-day period.
Shortage and emergency requested partial use one identical starting event merely because both say 72 hours.
The described Massachusetts requested-remainder pathway requires the same dispensing pharmacy.
A partly dispensed Schedule II order is not an initially unfilled EPCS for the one-time initial-transfer pathway.

records.stem:
Case A: An otherwise eligible out-of-state Schedule II prescription is first presented on day 8 after issuance, and staff attempt to use the general 30-day rule instead of the applicable initial five-day rule.

Case B: A different eligible out-of-state prescription had a lawful requested initial partial fill within the five-day window, and a remainder is sought at the same pharmacy within 30 days of issuance.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every Massachusetts-issued Schedule II requested partial must begin within five days.
The second remainder is evaluated using the separate issuance-based remainder clock and other conditions.
The first prescription cannot be revived by replacing the applicable initial five-day condition with the general 30-day rule.
The remainder period is not a fresh 30 days from the initial partial fill.

records.stem:
Case A: A Schedule IV prescription allows two refills; after both are used, staff add three more because the law's maximum is five.

Case B: A Schedule V prescription in Massachusetts is treated as having no state refill-count limit because federal Schedule III-IV wording does not name Schedule V.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The maximum does not supply additional refills that the prescriber has not authorized.
A prescriber cannot authorize fewer refills than the law's maximum.
Federal III-IV wording proves Massachusetts has no five-refill limit for Schedule V.
The original dispensing counts as one of the five refills in every case.

records.stem:
Case A: A Schedule III prescription is first filled several months after issuance, and staff start the six-month refill clock on that first-fill date.

Case B: After a lawful transfer, the receiving pharmacy proposes another fresh six-month period beginning with transfer.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Transfer renews the prescription for six additional months.
Unused refills can be dispensed after expiration simply because some remain.
Writing 'PRN' removes the six-month and refill-count limits.
The stated refill window runs from the original issue date.

records.stem:
Case A: Within the legal window, a prescriber adds an allowed oral refill authorization to a Schedule IV order, and staff omit the new authorization record.

Case B: One authorized quantity is supplied in two partial transactions, and the system records two new full refill authorizations as used.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every III-V partial remainder must follow the Schedule II shortage 72-hour rule.
Partial filling permits exceeding the authorized total if each transaction is small.
The later authorization must be recorded and remain within the applicable total, time, and quantity limits.
Every partial transaction necessarily consumes a complete new refill authorization.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy transfers a Schedule III refill but leaves the same remaining authorization active for dispensing at both pharmacies.

Case B: The pharmacies calculate the specific transfer-record retention period from the transfer date rather than the last refill date.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The transfer record must prevent duplicate use of the same remaining authorization.
The word 'TRANSFER' alone supplies all required receiving-pharmacy information.
The refill-transfer rule's retention clock is necessarily the same transfer-date clock as initial EPCS transfer.
Only the receiving pharmacy retains records; the sending pharmacy may discard its copy immediately.

records.stem:
Case A: At the patient's request, two DEA-registered retail pharmacies arrange an eligible initial transfer of a never-dispensed electronic Schedule II prescription where state law permits it.

Case B: To accomplish the transfer, staff print the prescription and fax the printout while changing part of its signed content.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Associated III-V refills must remain separately active at the originating pharmacy.
Only the recipient keeps initial-transfer records, beginning at a future last refill.
Printing, faxing, and changing signed content preserve the required electronic-transfer form.
The described initial unfilled EPCS pathway is possible on a one-time basis under its conditions.

records.stem:
Case A: A never-filled Schedule III prescription originally received on paper is scanned, and staff attempt to use the original-unfilled-EPCS transfer rule.

Case B: A separate never-filled Schedule VI prescription originated on paper, and staff assume the controlled EPCS format restriction prohibits its Massachusetts transfer too.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every unfilled Schedule VI transfer is prohibited unless the original was electronic.
Authority to transfer Schedule VI necessarily includes authority to transfer Schedule III.
Scanning does not qualify the first prescription as an originally electronic prescription for that pathway.
A Schedule VI transfer revives an expired order regardless of authorization.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist queries a patient's MassPAT history and concludes that the pharmacy no longer needs to submit that day's dispensing data.

Case B: The pharmacy has an active reporting account, but the dispensing pharmacist has not maintained the required access credentials.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A clinical query does not substitute for pharmacy dispensing-data submission.
Having valid MassPAT credentials permits curiosity searches unrelated to patient care.
Every prescriber query mandate automatically applies identically to every dispensing pharmacist transaction.
An active pharmacy reporting account eliminates the dispensing pharmacist's access requirement.

records.stem:
Case A: A prescriber is about to prescribe an applicable Schedule II opioid and proposes skipping the required PMP check because the pharmacy will submit dispensing data later.

Case B: Staff conclude that gabapentin's inclusion in dispensing reports automatically places it in every specifically enumerated opioid or benzodiazepine query category.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Reporting inclusion alone does not establish every other category-specific query trigger.
Holding a pharmacist license exempts the person from duties arising when legally prescribing.
Drug schedule and opioid or benzodiazepine classification are separate facts relevant to the rule.
Later pharmacy reporting does not fulfill the prescriber's applicable pre-prescribing query obligation.

records.stem:
Case A: A Massachusetts pharmacy excludes gabapentin from dispensing reports solely because it is not federally scheduled.

Case B: A prescription is prepared but not yet sold or delivered, and staff enter the preparation date as though it necessarily proves actual delivery.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A pharmacy's out-of-state location automatically removes Massachusetts reporting duties for shipments into the state.
Preparation and actual sale or delivery are distinct events that must be accurately represented.
The special reporting inclusion does not make every Schedule VI medicine reportable in the same way.
Gabapentin is included in the described Massachusetts reporting framework despite its Schedule VI classification.

records.stem:
Case A: An adult agent collects a reportable controlled prescription for another person, and staff record an old identifier belonging to the patient instead of inspecting the applicable recipient identification.

Case B: A clerk proposes using the customer's Social Security number as the PMP customer identifier.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The actual receiving ultimate user or agent and applicable current identification must be considered.
Schedule VI classification alone exempts gabapentin from the Additional Drug identification requirements.
A delivery ID exception authorizes untracked delivery to any recipient.
The Social Security number is the preferred substitute for an applicable government-issued customer identifier.

records.stem:
Case A: A patient lacks the usual identifier, and the pharmacist has documented reason to believe failure to dispense would cause serious hardship.

Case B: Staff propose using the exception without collecting the substitute name, address, and signature information or marking the exception appropriately.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The exception permits leaving all identity and reporting fields blank.
Naloxone and gabapentin necessarily have identical customer-ID rules because both appear in reporting guidance.
Every person without ID must be handled identically without reviewing hardship conditions.
The described case-by-case exception requires professional judgment and documentation of the hardship reason.

records.stem:
Case A: An adult's first outpatient opioid prescription exceeds the basic seven-day limit with no documented applicable exception, while staff call it a routine later refill.

Case B: The pharmacy knows of an applicable voluntary non-opiate directive but assumes a general prescription-validity presumption permits ignoring that knowledge.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A minor's subsequent opioid prescriptions are exempt from the basic limit solely because they are subsequent.
Writing 'chronic pain' alone necessarily fulfills every exception and documentation condition.
The first-outpatient situation must be assessed under its actual seven-day rule and applicable exception conditions.
Knowing about the directive is irrelevant whenever a written prescription exists.

records.stem:
Case A: The pharmacy's internal record has correct directions, but the patient container label omits them.

Case B: Staff insist every field required on the original prescription, including the prescriber's DEA number, must automatically be printed on every patient label.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Original-prescription fields and patient-label fields must be checked under their own requirements.
A correct internal record does not cure missing required information on the patient label.
Attaching a technician-prepared label transfers final validation responsibility to the technician.
The actual dispensed product must be identifiable through the appropriate drug, strength, and form information.

records.stem:
Case A: An eligible patient requests large-print directions, and staff equate the statute's characters-per-inch requirement with a 10-point font size.

Case B: A compounded prescription is labeled without identifying it as a sterile or nonsterile compounded preparation as applicable.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The compounded preparation's BUD is simply the source manufacturer's expiration in every case.
An inpatient label exception removes the same requirements for every outpatient prescription.
Compounding identification is unnecessary whenever the ingredient is an approved drug.
Characters per inch and point-size units are not interchangeable measures.

records.stem:
Case A: Staff interpret the federal warning against giving a controlled medicine to another person as prohibiting an otherwise lawful pharmacist-to-pharmacist transfer of prescription information.

Case B: A pharmacy applies that federal Schedule II-IV label warning as a mandatory federal requirement to every Massachusetts Schedule VI medicine.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every drug in every schedule has an identical opioid-information duty.
Any leaflet automatically satisfies the designated opioid-information requirement.
The patient-to-person drug warning and prescription-information transfer govern different acts.
Every Massachusetts Schedule VI label must bear the same warning by virtue of federal scheduling.

records.stem:
Case A: For an eligible protected-care Schedule VI prescription, the prescriber requests the permitted practice-name label treatment.

Case B: Staff apply the same Schedule VI exception to testosterone and delete the actual prescriber identity from the pharmacy's original record.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Using a practice name means prescriber-identity verification is no longer necessary.
The eligible Schedule VI request must be assessed under the specific practice-name label pathway.
The Schedule VI label exception authorizes both the testosterone label change and erasure of internal prescriber identity.
Use in gender-affirming care makes every medicine Schedule VI.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacist substitutes an extended-release product for an immediate-release product solely because the active ingredient name matches.

Case B: Another substitution decision relies on an A-rating somewhere in a product list without matching the relevant reference product and equivalence code.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Matching ingredient names alone does not establish interchangeability across release formulations.
Any A-rated entry proves every product with that ingredient is mutually interchangeable.
The terms pharmaceutical equivalent and therapeutic equivalent have no distinct requirements.
The insurer's preferred product is legally interchangeable solely because the claim pays.

records.stem:
Case A: An otherwise applicable Massachusetts brand prescription has no lawful no-substitution direction, and a less-expensive reasonably available interchangeable product is identified.

Case B: After dispensing the substitute, staff leave the label identifying only the originally prescribed product rather than what was actually supplied.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The label must identify the actual product dispensed under the applicable interchange labeling requirements.
The pharmacy can record the prescribed product instead of the actual product for convenience.
No-substitution must be a valid separate instruction rather than a default assumption from the signature.
The applicable Massachusetts selection rule must be applied rather than ignored for inventory convenience.

records.stem:
Case A: A prescription uses a generic drug name without specifying a manufacturer, and staff apply every brand-interchange assumption without reviewing the separate generic-name rule.

Case B: A product is described as an authorized generic marketed under a brand NDA, and staff reject that possibility solely because no separate ANDA entry is found.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Appearance on a listing guarantees current distribution and stock availability.
An authorized generic may be marketed under the NDA rather than a separate ANDA.
Actual product correspondence must be verified rather than assumed from the manufacturer name.
The generic-name selection pathway must be read on its own terms and with the prescriber's intent.

records.stem:
Case A: A genuine medical emergency meets the described exception conditions, and the prescribed no-substitution brand is unavailable while an eligible less-expensive interchangeable product is available.

Case B: The pharmacy uses the exception but omits the emergency date, hour, nature, and purchaser's written acceptance.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An emergency removes the described documentation and written-acceptance requirements.
The specified emergency pathway must be distinguished from routine disregard of a no-substitution instruction.
Every out-of-stock situation is automatically a medical emergency.
The emergency interchange pathway allows substituting any drug in the same therapeutic class.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy treats approval as a biosimilar as sufficient by itself to establish pharmacist-level substitution authority.

Case B: For an otherwise eligible biological substitution, staff import another state's fixed five-business-day notification rule as the Massachusetts statutory deadline.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Biosimilar approval and the required interchangeability determination are distinct.
The actual dispensed product must be identified and the required patient written notification provided.
The biological-substitution record rule permits ignoring every other applicable retention rule.
The Massachusetts reasonable-time wording should not be replaced by an unsupported other-state fixed number.

records.stem:
Case A: At checkout, an applicable prescription's retail price is lower than the amount the customer would otherwise pay through the described insurance cost-sharing transaction.

Case B: Staff assume that a paid claim automatically establishes the correct amount to collect without considering the Massachusetts lesser-price requirement.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The comparison can substitute an unrelated product's advertised price for the actual transaction.
The rule guarantees identical prices for all products and all insurance arrangements.
A paid claim conclusively proves compliance with the patient-charge rule.
The applicable lesser-price requirement must be evaluated before collecting the higher amount.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy selects a tamper-evident blister package and assumes its visible opening evidence proves child-resistant performance.

Case B: Staff classify every OTC product as exempt from special packaging without evaluating the listed substance, amount, or formulation.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every OTC product is exempt from special packaging solely because no prescription is needed.
A child-resistant container guarantees that no child can open it.
Tamper evidence and child resistance are distinct packaging properties.
Packaging rules are determined only by the shelf where the product is displayed.

records.stem:
Case A: A patient makes a documented blanket request for non-child-resistant packaging for their own prescriptions.

Case B: A prescriber requests non-child-resistant packaging for one prescription, and staff apply it to every future prescription from every prescriber.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The pharmacy may infer an unlimited waiver from an undocumented single transaction.
The patient's own blanket request must be distinguished from a request limited to one prescription.
Every older patient is automatically deemed to have requested non-child-resistant packaging.
A prescriber request for one prescription automatically covers all future unrelated prescriptions.

records.stem:
Case A: A package contains 21 prednisone 5-mg tablets and no other substance subject to the relevant prescription-drug special-packaging provision.

Case B: A second otherwise comparable package contains 22 prednisone 5-mg tablets; staff consider only the 5-mg tablet strength when evaluating the exception.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first package totals 105 mg and meets the stated package-total threshold for that prednisone exception.
Exceeding this product threshold automatically proves that no other lawful packaging exception can exist.
The second package meets the threshold because each tablet is only 5 mg.
The prednisone threshold applies without regard to other regulated ingredients in the package.

records.stem:
Case A: Staff extend the sublingual nitroglycerin packaging exception to every nitrate formulation, including products outside the stated exception.

Case B: A potassium supplement is in unit-dose form, and the reviewer compares its per-unit amount to the stated 50-mEq threshold rather than treating all potassium packages alike.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Any isosorbide dinitrate formulation at any strength meets the named exception.
Moving any mnemonic-packaged product into another container preserves the same exception without review.
The potassium exception ignores dosage form and applies to any amount in a bulk bottle.
The sublingual nitroglycerin exception does not exempt every nitrate formulation.

records.stem:
Case A: A patient requests a reusable dose planner, and the pharmacy proposes filling it with medication previously dispensed by a different pharmacy under the pharmacy-packaging pathway.

Case B: The patient's old closure still clicks shut, and staff take that as proof that child-resistant performance and product stability are preserved.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The planner's maximum supply period guarantees stability for every included medicine.
Closing mechanically does not prove required child-resistant performance or product stability.
The described pharmacy dose-planner pathway does not permit using medication previously dispensed by a different pharmacy.
A non-child-resistant request does not waive light, moisture, or other stability protection.

records.stem:
Case A: A seller leaves regulated pseudoephedrine product openly accessible to customers without the described behind-counter or locked-storage process.

Case B: A single sales package qualifies for the specified 60-mg-or-less logbook exception, and staff apply it as an exemption from every quantity and sale requirement.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The narrow logbook exception does not erase every other applicable sales condition.
A pharmacy license alone replaces the separate regulated-seller training and certification framework.
Required logbook entries are retained for at least the specified two years.
The described controlled-access storage and staff-provision requirements still apply to the sale pathway.

records.stem:
Case A: Under the described Massachusetts syringe advisory, staff refuse a hypodermic-syringe sale solely because the customer has no prescription or ID.

Case B: The customer concludes that permission to buy the syringe also permits purchasing any prescription medicine to put in it without an order.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every Schedule V product may be sold OTC in Massachusetts solely because of its schedule.
The advisory's appropriate use and disposal information should be distinguished from a new invented quantity cap.
The cited Massachusetts advisory allows the described syringe or needle sale without prescription or ID.
Device access does not authorize dispensing the separate prescription medication without its required order.

records.stem:
Case A: An extralabel drug is dispensed for a food-producing animal without the applicable withdrawal or withholding instructions.

Case B: A Veterinary Feed Directive is treated as an ordinary human Schedule VI prescription with freely renewable extralabel feed use.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Food-residue precautions and required withdrawal or withholding information remain relevant.
AMDUCA automatically authorizes every compound from any bulk active ingredient.
A patient-name exception permits omitting all animal identification and use directions.
A VFD permits unrestricted extralabel feed use under ordinary human Schedule VI refill rules.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy performs a rapid test but changes the manufacturer's specimen and timing instructions while assuming its original waived status remains unchanged.

Case B: The pharmacy obtains samples marked not for resale and adds them to ordinary paid prescription inventory.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Drug samples marked not for resale are not ordinary retail inventory for resale.
The word waived eliminates any testing-site certificate or procedure obligation.
Changing test instructions can affect waived status and requires the appropriate complexity and certificate analysis.
Obtaining a test result does not independently create diagnostic or prescribing authority.

records.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy uses the current paper Form 222 but combines orders for two suppliers on the same form and relies on obsolete triplicate-copy instructions.

Case B: A supplier partially fulfills an eligible order and proposes starting the 60-day completion period at the first shipment rather than the order date.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: An expired registrant may keep ordering because unused forms remain.
The stated partial-shipment completion clock runs from the order date.
The purchaser preserves the required executed copy and records actual receipt quantities and dates.
The current described paper system is single-sheet and uses one supplier per form.

records.stem:
Case A: For the specified federal distribution calculation, a practitioner has 10,000 included distributed dosage units and 190,000 dispensed dosage units during the same calendar year.

Case B: With no other transactions changing the totals, another 1,000 included units are proposed for distribution; the practitioner continues to divide only by dispensed units or revenue.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first stated ratio is 10,000 divided by 200,000, or exactly 5 percent.
Meeting the federal percentage eliminates all Massachusetts and supply-chain requirements.
The practitioner may ignore an expected excess until after year-end reconciliation.
The proposed totals remain exactly 5 percent because the original calculation was 5 percent.
